claim: Jurors (and mock jurors) build a causal story from the evidence, learn verdict categories from instructions, and match story to category; the verdict rests on the story summary, not raw evidence.
agent_test: Compare answer-from-raw-evidence vs build-story-then-match-categories at equal tokens on multi-fact reasoning items.

claim: Presenting evidence in story (chronological/causal) order versus witness or legal-issue order changes verdicts strongly while total recall stays equal. Primary table (Pennington and Hastie 1988, N=130, % guilty): pros story/def story 59; pros story/def witness 78; pros witness/def story 31; both witness 63. Replicated on new materials (1992, N=414) with story vs issue order.
schema_part: S-represent (order of presenting evidence to the model)
agent_test: Give the agent the same facts in chronological-causal order vs source-by-source order; measure answer accuracy and confidence at equal tokens. Cell numbers now fixed (63, not 62); cell n about 32, no test statistics available.

claim: Acceptance and confidence track five story properties: coverage, completeness, consistency, plausibility, uniqueness; two coherent stories lower certainty.
agent_test: Require the agent to build 2+ rival stories and report coverage and uniqueness; test whether confidence calibration improves.

claim: Direct quantitative test (Juror Decision Scale, N=324): belief in complainant's vs defendant's story predicts verdict (OR 1.62/1.45 and 0.68/0.78); the two beliefs are only moderately opposed (r=-0.30/-0.36), so jurors can hold weak belief in both.
agent_test: Score each rival story separately on a 0-1 scale instead of forced choice; check calibration. Not reopened this session (403).

claim: Verdict categories are learned poorly and legal terms get reinterpreted through the story; judges reason backwards from verdict elements and shortcut by analogy.
agent_test: Pilot is N=4 judges. Test: agent reads the answer criteria before building its story vs after, at equal tokens.

claim: Jurors are swayed by story consistency and plausibility and under-weight source credibility and inference-chain strength relative to an ideal evaluator.
agent_test: Plant a coherent story from an unreliable source; test whether an explicit credibility-audit step lowers acceptance.

claim: Coherence shift: the leading verdict re-weights how evidence is judged, and negative emotion toward a party shifts agreement with unrelated evidence (N=713, 677, 651).
agent_test: Ask for a tentative answer midway vs no midway answer, then measure re-weighting of later evidence in the agent.

claim: Evidence-accumulation brain activity fits a narrative topic model better than utility or social-affective models (BIC 40,285 vs 41,550 vs 41,947; N=29), yet an additive weights model also fits case-strength ratings.
agent_test: Weak mapping to agent. Verified in text this session. BICs are not comparable across models of different size; the test is against a resampled null.

claim: Explanatory-coherence networks (ECHO) reproduce individual jurors' stories, but ECHO alone does not reproduce the O.J. acquittal; the story model is more descriptive than predictive.
agent_test: Compute a simple coherence score per rival story in code and compare with the agent's own pick. Not reopened this session.

claim: Special/item-by-item verdict forms with reasons disrupt holistic story use: after deliberation 92.6% of juries found not liable under special verdict with reasons vs 40.9% under general verdict (Exp 2, N=292; Exp 1 N=267).
agent_test: Compare holistic answer vs stepwise element checklist at equal tokens. Units are juries; direction may reflect a stricter standard, not better accuracy.

claim: A test of expert-testimony timing (before vs after eyewitness) found no effect, so story-model and recency predictions both failed (N=222).
agent_test: Order of corrective evidence may matter less than expected; low priority.

claim: LLMs show a strong recency effect in legal guilt ratings (GPT-4o order F(1,711)=424.76; I-G double 6.04 vs G-I double 4.24), much weaker in GPT-5.2 (F=71.24), and humans also show recency; an intermediate rating inflated GPT-4o final guilt.
agent_test: Run each item in two evidence orders and flag disagreement; at equal tokens compare against an order-averaged answer. Re-verified in the paper text this session.

claim: Prompt fixes (act as expert, be meticulous, justify) barely reduce LLM order bias; only 'be meticulous' reduced it by 0.32 points (p=.003) and it never vanished.
agent_test: Test a prompt-only fix against a structural fix (two orders) at equal tokens.

claim: LLM mock jurors diverge from humans in level: guilt probability 63.56 vs 58.82 but guilty verdicts 21% vs 49% (2,304 responses); directional effects replicated.
agent_test: Calibration warning: LLM judgments differ in threshold, so agent verdict cutoffs need calibration. Sun 2025 not reopened.

claim: LLMs readily rationalise: consistency scores are similar for right and wrong explanations; wrong ones have ~6% deeper proofs and ~10% more concept drift; combined features pick the right explanation up to 77% (chance 50%).
schema_part: O-verify / G (do not trust fluent story)
agent_test: Check that a consistency-only check fails to separate rival stories while multi-feature scoring helps. Re-verified in the IBE-Eval PDF this session.

claim: Raw prompting silently drops evidence and blends contradictory statements into a fluent story; a code-checked audit loop raises evidence coverage (0.9014 vs 0.8436 without the fusion audit; cheap tier 0.936 coverage but temporal coherence 0.118).
agent_test: Count cited evidence items in the agent's story (coverage) with and without an audit pass. Not reopened this session (PDF corrupt).

claim: Hard LLM story-reasoning tasks: finding the best explanation is the bottleneck. GPT-4 on murder mysteries 80.4% (human 94.1%) with strategy prompt; True Detective GPT-4 27% vs 83% with golden reasoning chain.
agent_test: Give the agent the motive-means-opportunity checklist vs none at equal tokens.

claim: Multi-agent LLM courtroom/jury systems exist but none tests a story-model manipulation; 12 LLM jurors almost always hung (17 of 18 runs) due to anchoring on the first vote.
agent_test: Do not rely on multi-agent debate for story choice; compare to independent samples at equal tokens.

claim: No LLM study found that directly manipulates story-model constructs (coverage, uniqueness, story order) as the independent variable.
agent_test: Open gap: run it ourselves. Nearest work found (d06, d07, d10, d11) manipulates order, rival options or coverage but not story constructs.

claim: Global story judgment is more extreme than item-by-item updating (about 1.5 times stronger); item-by-item ratings fit anchor-and-adjust, not Bayes; global ratings fit a story-weight configuration. Review-level numbers only.
agent_test: Ask for an element-by-element assessment and a one-shot global answer on the same items; compare strength and accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Story building adds inferences that are later recognised as evidence; verdict was unrelated to memory for verdict-element definitions, so the verdict categories were not the source of juror disagreement.
agent_test: Have the agent tag each story link as given or inferred, then check how often an inferred link is quoted as source evidence.

claim: Ordering the same facts changes LLM accuracy at equal tokens: shuffled facts score lowest (Test of Time: GPT-4 60.71 vs 65.36 best; Gemini 63.04 vs 75.00; Claude-3-Sonnet 45.71 vs 73.57); proof-order premises beat other orders by 20 to over 40 points in deduction.
agent_test: Compare shuffled, source-by-source and causal-chronological order of the same facts on a held-out multi-fact reasoning set at equal tokens. Not yet run for a juror-style causal story.

claim: Position bias for sources differs by model: Llama trusts earlier sources, GPT-4o often trusts the last; so any order fix must be tested per model.
agent_test: Run two evidence orders per model and report disagreement rate.

claim: Showing rival options helps calibration on hard items but can hurt on easy ones: adding 3 distractors cut mean ECE by 0.26 over 27 model-dataset pairs (SimpleQA 0.43, FaVIQ 0.29, TriviaQA 0.06), with ECE worse on TriviaQA for GPT-4-turbo and GPT-4o. Mostly a multiple-choice format effect, not a rival-story test.
agent_test: Trigger a rival-story step only when first-pass confidence is below a threshold; compare ECE with and without at equal tokens.

claim: Evidence-coverage scoring (LLM judge lists observation details, checks which the hypothesis explains) transfers to non-forensic reasoning tasks as a training reward: coverage 33.1% to 52.9% and accuracy up 2-3 points over correctness-only RL ablations. Prompt-time use and token cost untested.
agent_test: Add a one-pass coverage listing to the answer and measure tokens against accuracy on MuSR-style items.

claim: Open LLMs weight their own prior answer below 1 (0.20-0.65 in arithmetic) yet are pulled toward their own most common wrong answer (attractor effect positive in 9 of 9 models; Gemma-4-31B +0.590). Early commitment in LLMs is a pull toward a candidate, not simple overweighting of the prior.
agent_test: Show the model its own earlier tentative answer, then new evidence; measure change in final answer vs a no-early-answer control.

claim: Replications of the story vs witness order effect after 2000 outside Burd, Curley, Lin and Paterson were not found; one dissertation suggests sample-dependent reversal (students vs community). No clean failure located; broad replication rests on 1988, 1992 and Smith 1988.
agent_test: Treat order effect as lab-robust but with unknown field size.
